events.title: The DAO crowdsale

research.summary: The DAO launched a token sale on Ethereum beginning 30 April 2016 and raised more than 11.5 million ETH, then worth around $150 million.
research.significance: The DAO became an unprecedented blockchain crowdfunding and governance experiment, setting the stage for Ethereum's defining governance crisis.

sources.title: MakerDAO — DeFi History timeline
Ethereum.org — The DAO hack and Ethereum Classic

events.title: The DAO exploit

research.summary: An attacker exploited a recursive-call/reentrancy vulnerability in The DAO and began draining Ether into a child DAO.
research.significance: The exploit was the defining smart-contract security failure of early Ethereum and forced the community to confront whether code immutability should override asset recovery.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation — Critical Update re DAO Vulnerability
Ethereum.org — The DAO hack and Ethereum Classic

events.title: DAO fork and Ethereum Classic split

research.summary: At block 1,920,000, the Ethereum hard fork moved DAO-related Ether to a refund contract; miners opposed to the intervention continued the original chain, which became Ethereum Classic.
research.significance: The split permanently demonstrated that blockchains are also governed by communities and social consensus, not code alone.

sources.title: Ethereum.org — The DAO hack and Ethereum Classic
Ethereum.org — protocol timeline

events.title: Rare Pepes emerge on Counterparty

research.summary: The first Rare Pepe Counterparty collectible was posted in early September 2016, and the Rare Pepe Directory project was organized days later.
research.significance: Rare Pepes created a native blockchain collectible/art culture on Bitcoin before the Ethereum NFT boom.

sources.title: Book of Kek — Rare Pepe Series 1
Book of Kek — Rare Pepe Blockchain Project

events.title: Lightning Network paper proposes Bitcoin payment channels

research.summary: Joseph Poon and Thaddeus Dryja's Lightning Network paper proposed scalable off-chain instant Bitcoin payments routed through networks of payment channels.
research.significance: Lightning became Bitcoin's dominant second-layer payments architecture and a key answer in the block-size/scaling debate.

sources.title: Lightning Network paper

events.title: Second Bitcoin halving

research.summary: Bitcoin's second halving reduced the block subsidy from 25 BTC to 12.5 BTC on 9 July 2016.
research.significance: It reinforced Bitcoin's fixed issuance schedule and established halvings as recurring global market and mining events.

sources.title: Bitcoin.org — Halving history

events.title: Bitfinex hack

research.summary: Bitfinex suffered a security breach on 2 August 2016 in which 119,755 BTC were stolen.
research.significance: It was one of crypto's largest exchange thefts and later became remarkable for both BFX loss tokens and a massive law-enforcement recovery.

sources.title: Bitfinex — 2016 Security Breach FAQ

events.title: Zcash launches

research.summary: Zcash launched its Sprout mainnet on 28 October 2016 with zk-SNARK-based shielded transactions.
research.significance: Zcash brought production zero-knowledge privacy to a permissionless cryptocurrency and made advanced cryptography a mainstream crypto topic.

sources.title: Electric Coin Company — Zcash Launch and Roadmap

events.title: Parity/Ethereum ecosystem grows around smart-contract infrastructure

research.summary: Parity 1.0 launched in March 2016 as a Rust Ethereum client, and by late 2016 the Ethereum Foundation listed Parity alongside Geth, Ethereum Wallet/Mist and ethereumJ as clients users should update for network hard forks.
research.significance: The rise of multiple production Ethereum clients made client diversity, performance and independent infrastructure teams an important part of Ethereum's architecture.

events.title: Ethereum Homestead upgrade marks a more mature network phase

research.summary: Ethereum's Homestead hard fork activated in March 2016, moving the network beyond its experimental Frontier phase.
research.significance: Homestead signaled increasing confidence in Ethereum's live smart-contract platform just before The DAO era.

sources.title: Ethereum Foundation — Homestead Release

events.title: Zcash trusted-setup ceremony becomes part of privacy-coin lore

research.summary: Six participants generated the Sprout zk-SNARK public parameters through a multi-party trusted-setup ceremony shortly before Zcash launched.
research.significance: The ceremony became legendary privacy-crypto lore because security depended on at least one participant destroying secret setup material.

sources.title: Zcash ceremony archive

events.title: MetaMask emerges as a key Ethereum browser wallet

research.summary: MetaMask was created in 2016 by Aaron Davis and Dan Finlay as a self-custodial Ethereum browser wallet/extension.
research.significance: MetaMask became the dominant consumer gateway to Ethereum dapps, DeFi and NFTs.

sources.title: MetaMask — origin story

events.title: Ethereum community debates immutability after DAO exploit

research.summary: Ethereum users, miners and developers debated soft forks, hard forks, immutability and social consensus after The DAO exploit.
research.significance: The debate is essential to understanding why the hard fork produced Ethereum Classic, but it is a period rather than one instant.

events.title: BitMEX popularizes perpetual swap trading

research.summary: BitMEX launched XBTUSD, which it described as the world's first perpetual Bitcoin/USD leveraged swap, with up to 100x leverage and no expiry.
research.significance: The perpetual swap became crypto's defining derivatives instrument and was later copied across virtually every major trading venue.

research.significance: Cryptsy became one of the major exchange collapses of the pre-ICO altcoin era and another warning about centralized custody and opaque exchange management.

events.title: SegWit proposal becomes center of Bitcoin scaling debate

research.summary: Segregated Witness was designed and specified through BIP141 and became a central issue in Bitcoin's scaling debate; mainnet deployment signaling was scheduled to begin 15 November 2016.
research.significance: SegWit addressed transaction malleability and expanded effective block capacity, becoming the core technical compromise around which the block-size war intensified.

events.title: Bitcoin Unlimited grows among big-block advocates

research.summary: Bitcoin Unlimited developed into a prominent alternative Bitcoin implementation during the block-size dispute. Its February 2016 v0.12 experimental release let node operators configure block-size acceptance/mining limits and added Xtreme Thinblocks for larger-block propagation.
research.significance: Bitcoin Unlimited embodied the large-block view that block-size policy should emerge from users and miners rather than remain fixed by the reference implementation, helping set up the 2017 block-size climax.

events.title: Antminer S9 becomes an iconic Bitcoin mining machine

research.summary: Bitmain announced the Antminer S9 on 31 May 2016, advertising 14 TH/s at about 1,375 watts and calling it the first commercially available Bitcoin miner built on a 16nm process; first-batch shipping was scheduled for 12 June.
research.significance: The S9 became one of the most recognizable and long-lived ASIC generations and helped define industrial Bitcoin mining through the next market cycle.

events.title: Australian media reports Craig Wright's Satoshi claim

research.summary: Craig Wright publicly claimed that he was Bitcoin creator Satoshi Nakamoto in coordinated interviews and a blog demonstration. Cryptographers and Bitcoin developers quickly disputed the public proof, and Wright abandoned a promised further proof days later.
research.significance: The episode became the most prominent Satoshi identity claim of the period and a lasting example of why cryptographic proof matters more than biography or media access.

sources.title: Ars Technica — Craig Wright publicly claims to be Satoshi
WIRED — Wright ends attempt to prove claim

research.notes: Never state that Wright was Satoshi. This row records a disputed public claim.

events.title: Gavin Andresen says he believed a Wright signing demonstration

research.summary: Gavin Andresen said he believed Craig Wright was Satoshi after a private London demonstration in which Andresen said Wright signed a message with a key associated with an early Bitcoin block. Andresen acknowledged he could have been deceived and later said trusting Wright had been a mistake.
research.significance: Andresen's endorsement gave Wright's claim unusual credibility and became one of the strangest episodes in Bitcoin's Satoshi mystery.

sources.title: WIRED — How Craig Wright privately 'proved' his claim to Gavin Andresen
WIRED — Wright abandons public proof

events.title: Bitcoin Core commit access is removed from Gavin Andresen amid controversy

research.summary: Bitcoin Core maintainers revoked Gavin Andresen's ownership/write access to the project's GitHub organization after his endorsement of Craig Wright, citing concern that his account might have been compromised and the security risk of repository access.
research.significance: The move became a notable Bitcoin governance and software-security episode, showing that social trust and repository permissions sit alongside consensus rules in open-source protocol development.

sources.title: The Guardian — Bitcoin project blocks out Gavin Andresen
The Register — Andresen write access revoked

events.title: Ransomware economy increasingly standardizes on Bitcoin

research.summary: The FBI reported a clear rise in ransomware and noted that victims were increasingly being instructed to pay ransoms in Bitcoin rather than older prepaid-card methods.
research.significance: By 2016 Bitcoin had become closely associated with ransomware payments, setting the stage for globally disruptive attacks such as WannaCry in 2017.

events.title: BIP32 and hierarchical deterministic wallet practices become mainstream

research.summary: BIP32 was assigned on 11 February 2012 and specified hierarchical deterministic wallets, allowing a tree of public/private keys to be generated from a single seed.
research.significance: HD wallets radically simplified backups, account separation and key generation and became foundational wallet infrastructure.

research.significance: Multisig contract wallets became an early way for Ethereum organizations and groups to protect shared funds, while also introducing a new class of smart-contract custody risk.
